llm.summary: This code-refinement skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it includes under-disclosed external posting and instructions that can push agents past normal stop and scope limits.

dimensions.detail: The main purpose is coherent code-quality analysis and optional refactoring, but the included insight-generation module directs posting findings and code evidence to GitHub Discussions, which is a broader external disclosure capability than local refinement.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Execution modes can authorize broad repository changes, branch-size guard overrides, and resuming after harness stop signals; those instructions materially weaken normal user and platform control during high-impact code edits.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a markdown skill with markdown modules only; metadata and hashes match the supplied package context, and there is no install script, binary, or automatic persistence mechanism in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Read/grep/find commands are proportionate for code review, but repository-wide scans, optional execution of all findings, docs/refinement writes, commit-style closure tracking, and GitHub Discussions publication are broad for a general refactoring trigger set.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not create background services or credentials, but it instructs persistent repository modifications and synthesis documents, and it tells the agent to resume after stop signals when execution mode is active.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an aggressive refactoring workflow and are prepared to keep it tightly scoped. Avoid using phrases like "ignore scope guard," "execute all findings," or "do not stop" unless you genuinely want broad changes. Do not load or run the insight-generation module unless you explicitly intend to publish findings to GitHub Discussions after reviewing and redacting them.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Repository edits and closure tracking are expected when the user explicitly asks to apply refactoring findings, but the execution language is broad enough to warrant review guidance.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The instruction to resume after a harness stop signal is not necessary for code refinement and conflicts with normal execution boundaries.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The insight-generation module’s GitHub Discussions posting is an external publication flow that is not clearly disclosed in the main workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Posting findings externally may expose code locations and internal findings; this is not required for local quality analysis.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad triggers such as clean-code, craft, and anti-slop could activate a powerful workflow in ordinary developer conversation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The GitHub Discussions publication step lacks a clear user-facing warning or approval gate in the artifact text.
[SSD-1] unexpected: The ignore scope guard mode explicitly disables branch-size limits and can expand the blast radius of repository edits.
[SSD-4] unexpected: The completion-gate and stop-signal language attempts to keep execution going beyond ordinary interruption boundaries.
